title: Investigate: support/resistance zones disappear from the price chart once oscillators finish loading
description:
User-reported bug: on the Stock Detail page, the support/resistance zone bands (`PriceChart.tsx`'s support/resistance effect, `frontend-support-resistance-overlay`) render correctly on initial load, then disappear once `OscillatorChart` finishes loading its own data. Investigated the likely code path before writing this task, but did not reproduce live (no interactive browser session available while authoring this task) -- this is genuinely an investigation task, not a pre-diagnosed fix.

What's already known from reading the code:
- `PriceChart.tsx`'s support/resistance effect keys off `[historyQuery.data, analysisQuery.data, theme]` and re-adds/removes its `BaselineSeries` zone bands, false-breakout markers, and price lines on every dependency change via the effect's own cleanup function.
- `PriceChart` and `OscillatorChart` are separate sibling components (`StockCharts.tsx`), each presumably owning its own `createChart()` instance -- not obviously sharing one chart/pane, so a naive 'OscillatorChart's effect calls `chart.removeSeries` on PriceChart's own chart' theory seems unlikely on its face, but has NOT been ruled out (check whether they somehow share a chart/series ref, a context, or a ref passed down, rather than assuming full independence).
- `StockCharts.tsx`'s own doc comment mentions `PriceChart`/`OscillatorChart` 'start from the exact same DEFAULT_RANGE/DEFAULT_INTERVAL constants' and passes `errorSurfacedBySibling` between them -- meaning there IS some cross-component coordination already; check whether any of it could cause `PriceChart` to remount (not just re-render) when `OscillatorChart`'s own query settles, or whether `analysisQuery` is shared/refetched in a way that could momentarily return zones as empty/missing.

This task's job is to actually reproduce the bug (start the dev stack, load a ticker with visible support/resistance zones, watch what happens to them as the Oscillators panel finishes loading -- screenshot before/during/after via the same Playwright-plus-Read-tool-for-images technique used elsewhere in this codebase's own task history, since there's no interactive MCP browser tool available to a background agent), identify the actual root cause with confidence (not just a plausible theory), then fix it with a genuine regression test.

checklist.step: Reproduce the bug: start the dev stack, load the Stock Detail page for a ticker with visible support/resistance zones (check fixture data or a ticker known to have Elder-relevant zones), and screenshot the price chart at three points: immediately after the price chart itself renders zones, while the Oscillators panel is still loading, and once it has finished loading. Confirm the zones genuinely disappear (not just visually similar-looking) and note the exact moment it happens.

Identify the actual root cause by reading the relevant effect/render code directly (don't stop at a plausible theory) -- check whether `PriceChart` remounts, whether `analysisQuery.data`'s reference or content changes at that moment, whether any cleanup function fires unexpectedly, and whether `OscillatorChart`/any shared parent state is genuinely involved versus coincidental timing (e.g. both effects settling around the same moment for unrelated reasons).
Fix the identified root cause. Record the diagnosis and fix rationale as a `decisions` entry, including what was ruled out and why.

Add a regression test that would have caught this (mutation-test it: temporarily reintroduce the bug, confirm the test fails, then restore the fix) -- likely an integration-style test exercising both `PriceChart` and `OscillatorChart` together under the same parent, not just `PriceChart` in isolation, since the bug is specifically about their interaction.

decisions.decision: Root cause confirmed by live reproduction (headless Playwright against a real dev backend/frontend stack in fixture-data mode, ticker AAPL, with GET /api/stocks/AAPL/indicators artificially delayed via page.route so the exact moment it resolves could be isolated): the support/resistance zone bands disappearing is entirely internal to PriceChart.tsx -- OscillatorChart is NOT involved at all, and the 'once Oscillators finishes loading' framing is coincidental timing off a query PriceChart itself also depends on. PriceChart mounts its own chart/candlestick series in one effect, then five further effects independently add/remove overlay series onto that same pane: signal-overlay (EMA13/EMA26/channel bands plus a two-AreaSeries 'value zone' fill/mask pair), tide-region background shading, support/resistance zone bands (BaselineSeries), divergence, and kangaroo-tail. The zone-band effect depends only on [historyQuery.data, analysisQuery.data, theme] and commonly resolves (adding its BaselineSeries to the pane) BEFORE the signal-overlay and tide-region effects, which both depend on indicatorsQuery.data -- the same query OscillatorChart also depends on. Lightweight Charts draws a later-added series above an earlier one on the same pane (the same rule this file's own bringSeriesToFront/PR #151 comments already document for the candlestick series), so once indicators resolved, the signal-overlay effect's zoneBottomMaskSeries (an OPAQUE theme.palette.background.paper fill from valueZoneBottom down to the bottom of the pane) and the tide-region effect's full-pane-height AreaSeries got added AFTER the zone bands and painted over them -- confirmed experimentally by temporarily making zoneBottomMaskSeries transparent, which alone restored the lower zone bands' visibility in the same repro. Fixed by adding a zoneSeriesRef (tracking the currently-mounted zone-band series, alongside the existing chartRef/seriesRef pattern) that the signal-overlay and tide-region effects both consult: after adding their own new fill series, each re-asserts the zone bands' own z-order (bringSeriesToFront on each zone series) before finally moving the candlestick series to the front as before.
decisions.rationale: Mirrors the exact 'self-healing regardless of add/run order' idiom bringSeriesToFront's own doc comment already establishes for the candlestick-vs-fills problem (PR #151), extended to cover the zone-bands-vs-later-fills case that was never handled -- the smallest change consistent with the codebase's own established pattern for this exact class of bug, rather than inventing a new mechanism. Alternatives ruled out during investigation, before settling on this fix: (1) PriceChart remounting when OscillatorChart's query settles -- disproved by reading StockDetailPage.tsx (StockCharts is not conditionally keyed/remounted once analysisQuery.data is populated) and by the createChartMock call count staying at 1 throughout the regression tests; (2) analysisQuery.data's reference or content changing at that moment -- the zone effect's own dependency array doesn't include indicatorsQuery.data at all, so it never re-runs (and its BaselineSeries are never torn down) when indicators resolve; (3) PriceChart and OscillatorChart sharing a chart/series ref, a context, or any chart instance -- utils/chart.ts's createBaseChart is called independently by each and returns a fresh IChartApi per call, confirmed by reading both components' source directly; (4) theme identity changing on re-render -- main.tsx creates the MUI theme once at module scope and never recreates it, so useTheme() returns a stable reference across renders. Alternative fixes considered and rejected: making zoneBottomMaskSeries itself transparent/less opaque (would defeat its own documented purpose of erasing zoneTopSeries's fill below the value zone's lower bound); converting the zone effect to also depend on indicatorsQuery.data so it always re-runs last (would cause the zone bands to flicker/tear down and rebuild every time indicators refetch, for no benefit, and wouldn't fix the case where indicators resolve AFTER analysis on a slow network -- the actual reported scenario). Verified with a genuinely discriminating regression test in both PriceChart.test.tsx (unit-level, asserting the exact final z-order via a real-semantics setSeriesOrder mock) and StockCharts.test.tsx (integration-level, both PriceChart and OscillatorChart mounted together with GET /api/stocks/:ticker/indicators delayed, mirroring the originally reported symptom) -- both mutation-tested by reverting to the pre-fix code and confirming they fail, then restoring the fix and confirming they pass.
